theme: Destination demand proxies: US National Park Service visitation stats API, state park attendance, museum/theme-park attendance, ski resort data, beach visitation

candidates.name: npVisits
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed CSV 'All National Parks Visitation 1904-2016.csv' plus 'parks.csv' and 'parks_area.csv' (park metadata) and an R .Rda cache (parkVisits.Rda). Long annual NPS visitation series per park, 1904-2016, sourced originally from NPS IRMA stats system. R analysis script clean_data.R included.
candidates.why_useful: US domestic leisure-travel demand proxy going back over a century; useful as a long macro backdrop series for national-park-driven road-trip/leisure demand even though NPS's own API/IRMA portal (irma.nps.gov/STATS) is the live, current-vintage source. Not a numbered gap explicitly but supports category 6/regional travel-volume framing (gap 7 analog for domestic).
candidates.size_hint: single CSV, hundreds of parks x ~113 years

candidates.name: texas-state-parks
candidates.what_it_holds: Data/ directory with 5 committed Texas Parks & Wildlife monthly visitation Excel workbooks covering FY17 (Sep 2016-Aug 2017) through FY21 (Sep 2020-Jan 2021), 'all parks' monthly attendance reformatted from TPWD source releases. Includes a Jupyter notebook 'State Park Data Cleanup.ipynb'.
candidates.why_useful: State-level monthly park attendance panel spanning pre-COVID through pandemic reopening; a regional US leisure/staycation demand proxy that could triangulate with STR nights in Texas markets (Austin is in our Inside Airbnb panel).

candidates.name: national_park_visitation_analysis_w_mobile_phone_data
candidates.what_it_holds: Replication code for a published Scientific Reports paper (Alba, Pan, Yin et al. 2022) analyzing COVID-19 impact on US national park visitation by race/ethnicity using SafeGraph mobile-phone mobility data at Census Block Group level. Repo holds feature-extraction and modeling scripts under src/; only aggregated outputs are committed (raw SafeGraph data requires a commercial licence, not redistributed).
candidates.why_useful: Method/pipeline for turning SafeGraph-style mobility data into park-visitation demand estimates with demographic splits; useful as a template if the team ever gets SafeGraph/Placer.ai access, and as an academic anchor citation for mobility-based destination-demand nowcasting (relates to gap 17, nowcasting methods).
candidates.size_hint: code + aggregated results only, no raw mobility rows

candidates.name: SkiResortScraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Python web scraper targeting www.skiresort.info to pull global ski-resort details, statistics (slope km, lift counts, snow reliability ratings) and user reviews. No visitation/skier-day counts committed — it's a scraper against a third-party non-Airbnb site, not raw data in-repo.
candidates.why_useful: Could be run (as a method, not pre-built dataset) to build a global ski-resort attribute/rating panel as a winter-destination demand proxy; skiresort.info itself doesn't appear to publish skier-visit counts, only facility stats and ratings, so value is limited to a facility census rather than attendance volume.

candidates.name: SkiResort-Analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Exploratory analysis notebook/scripts over the output of SkiResortScraper (companion repo) -- resort attribute table (location, slope stats, ratings) for a global set of ski resorts scraped from skiresort.info, likely committed as a CSV in-repo alongside the analysis.
candidates.why_useful: Pairs with SkiResortScraper to give a ready-made global ski-resort facility census (not visitation counts) that could serve as a coarse index of winter-destination supply/popularity by region.
candidates.size_hint: unknown row count, single scrape snapshot

candidates.name: National-Park-Visitation-Forecasting
candidates.what_it_holds: Forecasting/exploration notebook over NPS visitation traffic; likely pulls from NPS's public visitation reports/IRMA stats system or a Kaggle mirror rather than shipping a large novel dataset. Not verified to have a large committed CSV beyond example data.
candidates.why_useful: Possible pointer to how to programmatically pull current NPS visitation figures (IRMA stats system, irma.nps.gov/STATS/SSRSReports) for a live, current-vintage US park-demand series; would need inspection of the code to confirm the exact pull method.

candidates.name: US-National-Parks-Visitation-Trends
candidates.what_it_holds: Streamlit app analyzing US national park visitation trends 2012-2022; likely bundles a CSV of annual visitation by park for that decade (unverified row-level detail) sourced from NPS public stats.
candidates.why_useful: A more recent (2012-2022) NPS visitation panel than kevinsoo/npVisits' 1904-2016 series would extend the domestic leisure-travel demand backdrop closer to the present, useful for cross-checking against STR/hotel demand cycles.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps kevinsoo/npVisits for 2012-2016 window but extends to 2022 if verified

candidates.name: us-national-park-visit
candidates.what_it_holds: Data visualization web app described as covering '44 years (1979-2023) of U.S. National Park visitation data' with interactive charts, maps and rankings; likely ships a processed CSV/JSON of annual visitation by park for that span (unverified exact file).
candidates.why_useful: If the underlying dataset is genuinely 1979-2023, it is a longer and more current NPS visitation panel than either kevinsoo/npVisits (ends 2016) or aliu82's 2012-2022 set, giving the most complete free domestic park-visitation backdrop found in this sweep.

notes: This theme is dominated by one-off student/coursework projects (SQL schema exercises, Tableau/PowerBI dashboards, toy 'Ski-Resort-Database' assignments with generated or fictional data) that hold no real attendance numbers -- these were excluded. No repo found for museum attendance or beach visitation at all (zero hits on direct searches); likely because those stats are not commonly redistributed on GitHub as CSVs -- the underlying government sources (state tourism offices, AAM museum industry surveys, NOAA/state beach-monitoring programs) would need direct API/scrape work, not a GitHub mirror. No working NPS IRMA Stats API client repo was found either, despite NPS publishing a public Data API (irma.nps.gov/STATS, and https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm) -- worth a human checking that API directly rather than via GitHub, since 'irma stats national park' and 'NPS visitation API' both returned zero repos. Ski-resort searches surface almost entirely fictional/generated 'Ski-Resort-Database' coursework with no real skier-visit counts; skiresort.info itself (target of the one real scraper found) does not appear to publish visitation numbers, only facility stats -- so ski-resort *attendance* data specifically looks absent from GitHub. Two NPS visitation repos (aliu82's 2012-2022 set and cat-grep's claimed 1979-2023 set) were flagged but not verified via directory listing (used up the api-call budget on the two most promising confirmed hits) -- worth a follow-up `gh api` directory check on those two before relying on them. Overall this theme sweep is thin: real committed destination-demand-proxy datasets on GitHub for this niche are rare; a human contact to NPS's own developer API and to Texas Parks & Wildlife / other state agencies directly would likely beat further GitHub searching.
